# {{name}}: a replay client generated by tabcap

Generated by `tabcap replay export-python` from bundle `{{bundleId}}` (session `{{session}}`). Regenerating overwrites this directory; do not edit `client.py` by hand.

## Contents

- `client.py`: one function per request group ({{functionCount}} in all). Recorded constants are written into the code; session values come from `Session` (a storageState file); timestamps are made at call time; parameters that change on every call are function arguments. The fields of the JSON responses are `TypedDict`s whose types are inferred from the recorded bodies: **an illustration only, the real responses decide**.
- `fixtures/`: the response body of each group's first sample; `index.json` holds what the tests expect (status, JSON keys, the fields equal in every sample).
- `conftest.py`, `test_replay.py`: tests that run against `tabcap replay serve`; they start no server themselves.

## Running against the replay server

[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) runs everything here: on first run it creates the environment (`.venv/`, plus `uv.lock`) from `pyproject.toml`, with httpx (HTTP/2 enabled) and, for the tests, the `test` dependency group (pytest).

```sh
tabcap replay serve <bundle> --port 4500 &   # listens on loopback only
TABCAP_REPLAY=http://127.0.0.1:4500 uv run --group test pytest -q
```

When the session cookies are needed, first `tabcap replay session <bundle> -o storage-state.json` (mode 0600, a real session: do not commit it), then add `TABCAP_STORAGE_STATE=storage-state.json`.

## Using the live browser session

To call the real site with the session the browser is logged in with (its cookies, the authentication headers its page sends, its localStorage / sessionStorage tokens), export it from the open tab while tabcap records (`tabcap net start` before the page makes its requests):

```sh
tabcap session export --for requests --out session.json   # mode 0600, LIVE credentials: never commit it
```

`_tabcap_session.py` (httpx only, no tabcap at runtime) turns the file into a client: `from _tabcap_session import load, client; s = load("session.json"); c = client(s)`; `s["storage"]["localStorage"]` holds the page's tokens. `tabcap session export --for httpx --out example_session.py` writes the same as a ready-to-import module instead. The export is a snapshot and expires with the session; small volumes are better left to the browser itself.

## What this client looks like on the wire

`tabcap wire probe --client <this directory>` compares what this client sends (TLS ClientHello, HTTP/2 settings, header order) with the Chrome for Testing tabcap launches, on a local echo at 127.0.0.1. It runs

```sh
uv run client.py wire-report --url https://localhost:<port>/client --ca <tabcap wire ca-path> --out report.json
```

which sends one GET with `Session()` exactly as generated, verifying the echo with its CA, and saves the echo's JSON report. Diagnostic only: the probe says which layer differs, not why a site answered the way it did.

## Route an existing scraper through the browser

`_tabcap_fetch.py` is not used by `client.py`. It is for a scraper you already have: instead of sending its requests itself, it hands each one to the running tabcap daemon (`POST /fetch`), and the session's logged-in tab sends it (its cookies, its CORS rules) and records it into the session's bundle, paced per host (config.json `fetch.minIntervalMs`, default 3000 ms between requests) and checked against stop rules.

```python
from _tabcap_fetch import TabcapFetch, Stopped, ListEnd, Waiting

tc = TabcapFetch(session="example")          # `tabcap net start --session example` first
status, headers, body = tc.fetch("https://example.test/api/list?page=2", stop_on=["json:$.code!=0"])
```

`Stopped` means a stop rule fired (or had fired) on the site: look at the response, then `tabcap guard resume --site <site>` when you decide to go on. `ListEnd` means an end rule matched (`end_on=[...]`, or `config.json` `sites.<site>.guard.endOn`, e.g. `json:$.code=203` for "no more pages"): the list has ended and nothing is stopped; it carries `status`, `headers` and `content`. `Waiting` means the session waits for the human (they took over the browser tab, or a verification page is up): nothing was sent; it carries `reason`, `next`, `session` and `url`, and ends when the human's agent runs `tabcap handoff continue` (or a `tabcap handoff wait --until-*` condition holds), after which you retry. Afterwards `tabcap bundle export har` and `tabcap replay export-python` turn the recording into fixtures for offline replay.

## Notes

- The default `base_url` is the origin of the recording; think about the account risk before calling a real site (docs/03 §4: offline replay first, sessions expire).
- Session values (`session.value(...)`) default to the recorded ones; override them with `Session(values={...})`.
- When the recording's account is bound to a proxy from the pool, the client must leave through the same proxy: `tabcap replay export-python <bundle> -o <dir> --proxy-env proxy.env` writes `TABCAP_PROXY_URL` into `proxy.env` (0600, carries the proxy credentials, never commit it); run `set -a; . ./proxy.env; set +a` before the client; `Session` reads that variable (no proxy without it).
- The generated clients do **not** read `http_proxy` / `https_proxy` / `NO_PROXY` (`trust_env=False`), so a machine-wide `NO_PROXY="[::1],…"` cannot break `httpx.Client` construction; the CA bundle still comes from `verify=` or `SSL_CERT_FILE`. To go through a proxy, set `TABCAP_PROXY_URL` or pass `proxy=` to `Session(...)` / `_tabcap_session.client(...)`; the argument wins over the environment variable.
